title: Cheaper OLEDs may be here even quicker than we thought as TCL CSOT says its new inkjet printing facility could be up and running as soon as this time next year
summary: Previous rumours had it penned for 2028.
body: TCL CSOT (the subsidiary of TCL that manufactures OLEDs and other panels) says its new inkjet-printed OLED factory has "entered the equipment move-in phase" (via TechPowerUp ) after the project "progressed at a rapid pace". In other words, it's started filling up its production facility with the equipment to produce inkjet OLEDs. Production, the company says, is targeted for about this time next year. What's the big deal, you ask? It all comes down to that phrase, "inkjet-printed". Inkjet printing (IJP) should be a much more cost-effective way of making OLED panels, which means it should ultimately deliver OLED gaming monitors that are cheaper than traditionally manufactured ones. Which is saying something, considering how much traditionally manufactured OLEDs have dropped in price over the past year—you can currently pick up a 240 Hz OLED monitor for just $269 at Walmart , for instance. body: Play This Right Now Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday. World of Warcraft: Forever is fascinating from so many perspectives—not necessarily in terms of what's on offer (it is, despite my enamorment, still very much Classic WoW) but in what it means for the MMO genre at large. It's the kind of project that usually only gets cooked up in "what ifs", a version of a 20-year old game that decided not to go for expansions, but to instead spread out horizontally .
